title: Issue briefs and reports
gist: An Atlantic Council index page of recent issue briefs whose teasers point to a severe Gulf energy shock: the Iran war closed the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline bypass was damaged by drones, and the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits at a four-decade low. Other teasers flag fragmenting globalization, Europe-Gulf economic ties and US-China tech competition in the Global South.

themes.theme: Hormuz closure and Gulf oil supply shock

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council brief teaser reports that after the Strait of Hormuz closed, Saudi Arabia rerouted more oil overland via its East-West Pipeline, which was then damaged by drone strikes while Iran-backed Houthis fired missiles near its Red Sea terminus.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Both the primary Gulf export route and Saudi Arabia's main bypass are compromised, implying acute crude supply risk.
insights.quote: First the Strait of Hormuz closed, so Saudi Arabia started sending more oil over land through its East-West Pipeline. Then drone strikes damaged the pipeline
insights.locator: The Saudi economy can hold out

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council issue brief by Khalid Azim argues the Saudi economy can hold out through the end of 2026 even if its oil exports fall to zero.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Saudi fiscal resilience reduces the odds of forced policy concessions, potentially prolonging an export disruption.
insights.quote: The Saudi economy can hold out through year’s end—even if oil exports drop to zero
insights.locator: The Saudi economy can hold out

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council brief notes the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to a four-decade low and warns that refilling it will become increasingly difficult as oil markets tighten.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: A depleted SPR limits Washington's ability to cap price spikes, and future refill buying adds demand to a tight market.
insights.quote: The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has reached a historic low. As oil markets continue to tighten, refilling the reserve will become increasingly difficult.
insights.locator: The risks of the strategic petroleum

insights.claim: Atlantic Council analysis frames European and Gulf states as sharing an interest in restoring energy flows cut off by the Iran war and reducing exposure to chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Chokepoint-avoidance infrastructure and energy-transition investment between Europe and the Gulf may gain policy support.
insights.quote: European and Gulf states share a strong interest in restoring the free flow of energy cut off by the Iran war
insights.locator: How Europe and the Gulf can

insights.claim: Atlantic Council analysis says boosting Europe-Gulf trade depends on progress on the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor and a free trade agreement, and asks whether Iran war disruption could revive these stalled projects.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Supply disruption could accelerate IMEC-linked logistics and infrastructure projects that had stalled.
insights.quote: Can the disruption caused by the Iran war provide an impetus to move these stalled projects forward?
insights.locator: Trade and connectivity in the Europe-Gulf

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council brief on the geoeconomics of Bretton Woods argues globalization is not ending but becoming more contested and fragmented as trade, finance, energy and critical minerals become entwined with national security.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Security-driven fragmentation favors friend-shoring, critical-minerals supply chains and higher structural costs rather than outright deglobalization.
insights.quote: But globalization is not ending—it is becoming more contested and fragmented.
insights.locator: The new geoeconomics of Bretton Woods

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council strategy paper argues that to prevail in the scientific and technological competition with China, the United States must strengthen tech-centric engagement with Global South countries.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: US tech diplomacy toward emerging markets may become a policy lever shaping AI and telecom market access.

insights.claim: An Atlantic Council report says Beijing is pressuring Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and the Philippines in the cognitive domain as well as with ships and aircraft, and that no multilateral mechanism defends against this.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Information-warfare pressure across the first island chain adds to Indo-Pacific geopolitical risk.
insights.locator: Building a multilateral cognitive warfare defense
